==English==
{{was wotd|2006|July|8}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|excentric|eccentrick|excentrick|qq2=obsolete|qq3=obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:bor|frm:excentrique<ety:der<la-med:eccentricus<ety:der<grc:ἔκκεντρος>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{bor|en|frm|excentrique}}, from {{der|en|la-med|eccentricus}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἔκκεντρος||not having the earth as the center of an orbit}}, from {{m|grc|ἐκ||out}} + {{m|grc|κέντρον||point}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|ex-|-centric}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪkˈsɛntɹɪk/|/ɛkˈsɛntɹɪk/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-eccentric.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-au-eccentric.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{hmp|en|excentric}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛntɹɪk|s=3}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}
[[File:Halley's Comet animation.gif|thumb|The orbit of [[w:Halley's Comet|Halley's Comet]] (denoted by the grey curve) is highly eccentric (sense 2).]]

# Not at or in the [[centre]]; away from the centre.
#: {{syn|en|eccentrical|excentrical}}
# Not [[perfectly]] [[circular]]; [[elliptical]].
#: {{syn|en|eccentrical|excentrical}} 
#: {{ux|en|As of 2008, Margaret had the most '''eccentric''' orbit of any moon in the solar system, though Nereid's mean eccentricity is greater.}}
# Having a different center; not [[concentric]].
#: {{syn|en|eccentrical|excentrical}}
# {{lb|en|figurative}} Of a person, [[deviating]] from the [[norm]]; behaving unexpectedly or differently; [[unconventional]] and slightly [[strange]].
#: {{syn|en|eccentrical|excentrical|odd|abnormal|see also [[Thesaurus:eccentric]]}}
#* {{RQ:William James Varieties|chapter=Lecture I|passage=There can be no doubt that as a matter of fact a religious life, exclusively pursued, does tend to make the person exceptional and '''eccentric'''.}}
# {{lb|en|physiology}} Of a [[motion]], against or in the opposite direction of contraction of a muscle (such as results from flexion of the lower arm (bending of the elbow joint) by an external force while contracting the triceps and other elbow extensor muscles to control that movement; opening of the jaw while flexing the masseter).
#: {{ant|en|concentric}}
# {{lb|en|figurative}} Having different [[goal]]s or [[motive]]s.
#: {{syn|en|eccentrical|excentrical}}
#* {{ante|1626}}, [[w:Francis Bacon|Francis Bacon]], '''1867''', Richard Whately (analysis and notes), James R. Boyd (editor), ''Essay XI: Wisdom for a Man's Self'', ''Lord Bacon's Essays'', [http://books.google.com.au/books?id=L3cw_0UPwnoC&pg=PA171&dq=%22his+own+ends,+which+must+needs+be+often+eccentric%22&hl=en&sa=X&ei=F_SnU9PEKc708QWQ74KIAw&ved=0CB0Q6AEwAA#v=onepage&q=%22his%20own%20ends%2C%20which%20must%20needs%20be%20often%20eccentric%22&f=false page 171],
#*: {{...}} for whatsoever affairs pass such a man's hands he crooketh them to his own ends, which must needs be often '''eccentric''' to those of his master or state: {{...}}
# {{lb|en|mycology}} Having or being an [[oospore]] with a single large oil globule on one side that displaces much of the [[ooplasm]] and forces the [[ooplast]]s to one side.
#: {{coord|en|centric|subcentric|subeccentric}}

====Usage notes====
* {{sense|physiology, of motion}} Motions that are eccentric or the opposite ({{m|en|concentric}}) are classified as {{m|en|isotonic||having equal tension}}, the antonym of which is {{m|en|isometric||retaining equal length}}. See also {{pedia|Isometric exercise}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# One who does not [[behave]] like others.
#: {{syn|en|character}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1989|author=Jeffrey Robinson|title=Rainier and Grace|page=26
|passage=A tiny, feisty woman who always spoke her mind, Charlotte was an '''eccentric''' in the wonderful way that some women from the last century were natural '''eccentrics'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1998|author=Michael Gross|title=Life On The Edge|pageurl=http://books.google.com.au/books?id=J5IwomfEGiEC&pg=PR9&dq=%22eccentrics%22&hl=en&sa=X&ei=TwOoU-HgKIbs8AWA4oDgAw&ved=0CNMCEOgBMDk#v=onepage&q=%22eccentrics%22&f=false|page=ix|year_published=2001
|passage='''Eccentrics''' live longer, happier, and healthier lives than conformist normal citizens, according to the neuropsychologist David Weeks.}}
# {{lb|en|slang}} A [[kook]]; a person of bizarre habits or beliefs.
# {{lb|en|geometry|astronomy}} A [[circle]] not having the same centre as another.
# {{lb|en|engineering}} A [[disk]] or [[wheel]] with its [[axis]] off centre, giving a [[reciprocating]] [[motion]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=George Saliba|title=Islamic Science and the Making of the European Renaissance|page=120|url=http://books.google.com.au/books?id=Boc0JjGRPF0C&pg=PA120&dq=%22eccentrics%22&hl=en&sa=X&ei=TwOoU-HgKIbs8AWA4oDgAw&ved=0CJgDEOgBMEY#v=onepage&q=%22eccentrics%22&f=false|passage=The discussion that revolved around the admissibility of '''eccentrics''' and epicycles lied{{sic}} at the core of this theoretical discussion, and those who would not allow such concepts took the position that such '''eccentrics''' and epicycles would then introduce a center of heaviness, other than the Earth, around which celestial simple objects would then move.}}
# {{lb|en|physiology}} An exercise that goes against or in the opposite direction of contraction of a muscle.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2021|author=Edward L. Wallace|title=Omniflex: A Unified System of Strength Training
|passage=Research tells us that '''eccentrics''', heavy partials, and static exercise may require several days or weeks of recovery time.}}

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|person who does not behave like others}} {{l|en|misfit}}, {{l|en|nonconformist}}; see also [[Thesaurus:maverick]]
* {{sense|person of bizarre habits or beliefs}} {{l|en|crank}}, {{l|en|odd duck}}, {{l|en|weirdo}}; see also [[Thesaurus:strange person]]
